City Through the Lens: Bangkok, Thailand

Local videographers reveal how they film their hometown — the real locations, permit hurdles, and techniques you won't find in guidebooks.

🎬 Real field footage: Insta360 X5 in Bangkok, Thailand

Quick Takeaways for Filmmakers

  • Best filming season: Hot year-round (35-40°C); monsoon May-Oct
  • Top 3 landmarks: Grand Palace, Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn), Chatuchak Weekend Market
  • Main airport: Suvarnabhumi
  • Drone rules: need Civil Aviation approval.
  • Featured camera: Insta360 X5

3 Must-Film Locations in Bangkok

1. Grand Palace

Filming Tip: Opens 8:30 AM; arrive early; cover shoulders/knees; no shorts.

2. Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)

Filming Tip: Best from Chao Phraya riverboat at sunset; climb steep steps carefully.

3. Chatuchak Weekend Market

Filming Tip: Sat-Sun only; 15,000 stalls; go 9 AM before heat peaks; handheld only.

Weather Reality Check

Hot year-round (35-40°C); monsoon May-Oct. Best Nov-Feb.

Pro tip: Plan your shoot dates around these conditions. The "best" months mean better light, fewer crowds, and more predictable weather windows.

Airport Transfer & Arrival Tips

Suvarnabhumi (BKK) 30min Airport Rail Link or Don Mueang (DMK) 40min bus.

Factor in transfer time when booking flights. Arriving early gives you buffer for gear checks and acclimatization before shooting.

Permits, Rules & Local Etiquette

Temples require respectful dress. Drones need Civil Aviation approval.

Remember: Always ask before filming people, especially in religious or residential areas. Respect local customs — it's the difference between getting great footage and being asked to delete it.
